mainTopic: An אשם תלוי that turns out to be unneeded, חיבת הקודש and food impurity, and a מנחה brought in a different pan or number of vessels than vowed
overview: The amud opens by finishing a משנה about an אשם תלוי, the offering brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned, for an owner who then learns he did not sin. The ruling depends on the stage he reached: before slaughter, after slaughter, or after the blood was sprinkled. רבי יוסי holds that even blood still in the cup is sprinkled and the meat is eaten. רבא explains this through רבי שמעון's rule that blood ready to be sprinkled counts as already sprinkled. Scholars in ארץ ישראל give a different reason: a כלי שרת sanctifies even disqualified items. רב אשי then asks why נותר and the פרה can become impure as food if they are as good as burned. רב כהנא answers that חיבת הקודש makes them able to become impure, and the גמרא adds that on the rabbinic level this impurity is even counted in levels. A new משנה then deals with someone who promised a מנחה in one kind of pan, or in one vessel versus two, and brought it differently. The גמרא explains why both kinds of change had to be taught, brings רבי שמעון's dissent, and has אביי explain that the vessel sanctifies the flour enough to become פסולה. Finally, אביי begins a new statement limiting the משנה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Before slaughter: the animal grazes and is sold
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה rules that if the owner finds out before slaughter that he did not sin, the animal grazes until it gets a blemish. It is then sold, and the money goes to gift offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: It should graze until it becomes blemished, then be sold, and its money goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a משנה about an אשם תלוי. This part says what to do with the animal if the owner learns, before it was slaughtered, that he never sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal was set aside as holy, so it cannot simply go back to being an ordinary animal. But it also cannot be offered as an אשם, because there is no sin for it to atone for. So it waits until it gets a blemish, is sold, and the money is used for communal gift offerings (נדבה).

keyTerms.meaning: A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he committed a sin
Becomes blemished, which makes it unfit for the altar
Its money (its value), not its blood
A voluntary gift offering; here the money goes toward communal gift offerings

phrases.english: It should graze until it becomes blemished
and it is sold
and its money is allocated for gift offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a משנה that the גמרא is quoting, which will be used against רב אשי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם תלוי that is not needed, discovered before slaughter, grazes until blemished, is sold, and its money goes to נדבה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: offer it anyway
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that the animal should be offered anyway, since it will atone for some other sin the person surely committed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: it should be offered, because if it does not come for this sin, it comes for another sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the previous ruling and says the animal can still be brought as an offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is that every person has some unknown sin. So the offering is never truly pointless, and it does not need to be retired.

keyTerms.meaning: He should offer it on the altar
A different sin

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: It should be sacrificed,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם אֵינוֹ בָּא עַל חֵטְא זֶה
phrases.english: since if it does not come for this sin,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא בָּא עַל חֵטְא אַחֵר.
phrases.english: it comes for a different sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion within the same quoted משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the אשם תלוי is offered anyway, as an atonement for some other unknown sin.

steps.title: After slaughter: spill the blood and burn the meat
steps.stepSummary: If the owner finds out only after slaughter that he did not sin, the blood is spilled out and the meat is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If after it was slaughtered he found out, the blood is spilled and the meat is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a later stage: the animal was already slaughtered when the person learned he did not sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now selling the animal is no longer possible, and it is not a valid offering. So it is treated like a disqualified offering. The blood is not put on the altar, and the meat is burned rather than eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Is spilled out (poured away instead of being put on the altar)
Is burned, as is done with a disqualified offering

phrases.english: If, after it was slaughtered, it became known to him —
phrases.notes: What he found out is that he never actually sinned.

phrases.english: the blood should be spilled,
and the meat should be burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the quoted משנה from the case before slaughter to the case after slaughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he discovers after slaughter that he did not sin, the blood is poured away and the meat is burned.

steps.title: After sprinkling the meat is eaten; רבי יוסי says even blood in the cup
steps.stepSummary: If the blood was already sprinkled, the meat is eaten. רבי יוסי says the same applies even if the blood was still in the cup: it is sprinkled and the meat is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blood was sprinkled, the meat is eaten. רבי יוסי says: even if the blood is in the cup, it is sprinkled and the meat is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the last stage, where the blood was already sprinkled. Then רבי יוסי adds a more lenient opinion about blood still sitting in the cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the blood is on the altar, the offering is complete, so the meat is eaten as usual. רבי יוסי pushes this earlier: blood that was collected and is waiting in the cup is treated as if it were already sprinkled. This is the key point that רבא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood was sprinkled on the altar
The cup (vessel) in which the blood was collected
Is eaten

phrases.english: If the blood was sprinkled — the meat is eaten,
and Rabbi Yosei says:
even if the blood is in the cup —
it is sprinkled and the meat is eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ הַדָּם בַּכּוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the stages in the משנה and adds רבי יוסי's lenient view, which sets up רבא's explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After sprinkling, the meat is eaten. רבי יוסי says the same applies even while the blood is still in the cup.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not saying the meat was already permitted before the sprinkling happened. He says that, because the blood is ready in the cup, it is still sprinkled and the meat is still eaten, even though the person now knows he did not sin.

steps.title: רבא: רבי יוסי follows רבי שמעון's rule that ready blood counts as sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי יוסי holds like רבי שמעון: blood that stands ready to be sprinkled is treated as already sprinkled. This goes against רב אשי's position.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: רבי יוסי said this following רבי שמעון's view, who says that anything standing to be sprinkled is considered as if it were sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the reason behind רבי יוסי's ruling. The גמרא brings this explanation as a difficulty against רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood in the cup is about to be sprinkled, so under רבי שמעון's rule it already counts as sprinkled. The meat then has the status of meat from an offering whose blood was sprinkled. רב אשי held that blood ready to be sprinkled is not automatically treated as sprinkled when it comes to the meat's status, so רבא's explanation clashes with his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Following the approach or opinion of
Whatever stands ready to be sprinkled is treated as already sprinkled

steps.whatToRemember: The rule כל העומד לזרוק כזרוק דמי (רבי שמעון) explains רבי יוסי's ruling. Because the blood is in the cup, the meat is treated as if the blood were already sprinkled. This is what challenges רב אשי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule of עומד לזרוק can decide the status of the meat itself, not just the blood. That is exactly the point רב אשי disputed.

phrases.english: And Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said it following the opinion of Rabbi Shimon,
who said: anything that stands to be sprinkled —
is considered as if sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי יוסי's view from the quoted משנה and turns it into a challenge against רב אשי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's view that blood standing to be sprinkled is not necessarily treated as sprinkled for the status of the meat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי, following רבי שמעון, lets the meat be eaten because the blood in the cup counts as sprinkled. This shows that עומד לזרוק does affect the meat, which contradicts רב אשי.

steps.title: A different reason for רבי יוסי: service vessels sanctify
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that רבי יוסי's ruling rests on רבי שמעון's rule. Scholars in ארץ ישראל explain that רבי יוסי holds a כלי שרת makes even disqualified items fit to be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really the reason? In the West, they say in the name of רבי יוסי בר חנינא that רבי יוסי's reason is this: he holds that service vessels sanctify disqualified items so they may be offered, even from the outset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's explanation from step 5 and offers a completely different reason for רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said רבי יוסי agrees with רבי שמעון that blood ready to be sprinkled counts as already sprinkled. The new reason has nothing to do with that rule. Since the blood is already inside a כלי שרת, the vessel's holiness makes it fit to be sprinkled even though the owner never sinned. This also removes the clash with רב אשי from step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that really the reason? A way of rejecting a proposed explanation.
In the West, meaning the scholars of ארץ ישראל
Service vessels used in the בית המקדש
They sanctify disqualified items
To be offered from the outset, not just בדיעבד

phrases.english: Is that the reason?
phrases.notes: This is aimed at רבא's explanation from the last step, that רבי יוסי follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: They say in the West
in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina:
this is the reason of Rabbi Yosei,
that he holds service vessels sanctify
disqualified items, to be offered from the outset.
phrases.notes: Here the blood is already sitting in the cup, which is a כלי שרת, so the vessel's holiness is what lets it be sprinkled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's explanation from step 5 and replaces it with a different reason.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רבא's reason for רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי's ruling itself stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no need to tie רבי יוסי to רבי שמעון's rule. The holiness of the כלי שרת explains the ruling on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, כלי שרת sanctify disqualified items to be offered even from the outset.

steps.title: If it is about to be burned, isn't it just dust?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks רב כהנא a question. רבי שמעון says what is about to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled, and the same should apply to what is about to be burned. So why can נותר and the פרה אדומה become impure as food, if they are as good as ashes?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: רבי שמעון said that anything about to be sprinkled counts as already sprinkled. So anything about to be burned should also count as already burned. Then why do leftover sacrificial meat and the red heifer become impure with the impurity of food? They are just dust!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes רבי שמעון's rule one step further, from sprinkling to burning. He uses this to challenge another ruling of רבי שמעון about food impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'about to be done' counts as 'already done,' then נותר and the פרה, which must be burned, should count as ash right now. Ash is not food, so it should not be able to receive טומאת אוכלין. Yet רבי שמעון rules that they do become impure as food, and that looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything about to be burned counts as already burned
Sacrificial meat left past its time to be eaten, which must be burned
The פרה אדומה (red heifer), which is burned to make ashes
The impurity that applies to food
Mere dust

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
Since Rabbi Shimon said
anything that stands to be sprinkled is as if sprinkled,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעוֹמֵד לִשְׂרוֹף נָמֵי כְּשָׂרוּף דָּמֵי –
phrases.english: then anything that stands to be burned is also as if burned.
So leftover meat and the heifer, why
do they become impure with the impurity of food?
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון's ruling, which the גמרא brought earlier on 101b.

phrases.english: They are mere dust!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא: מִדְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up רבי שמעון's rule from step 5 and turns it against another ruling of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that נותר and the פרה can become impure as food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'about to be burned' counts as 'burned,' these items are already like ash, and ash is not food, so it cannot receive טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: Regard for holiness makes them able to become impure
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that חיבת הקודש, the special regard for holy things, is what makes these items able to become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: the regard for holy things makes them susceptible to impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers רב אשי's question in a few words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that, by רבי שמעון's rule, these items are like ash. Their impurity does not come from being normal food. It comes from their holiness, because holy things are treated with extra care and can become impure even when ordinary rules would not allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Special regard for holy things, which makes them able to become impure
Makes them able to receive impurity

steps.whatToRemember: חיבת הקודש can make a holy item able to become impure even when it would not normally count as food.

phrases.english: He said to him: regard for holiness renders them susceptible.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב כהנא, answering רב אשי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a separate source for the impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The items could only become impure if they still count as real food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their holiness alone makes them able to become impure.

steps.title: Can holiness also make it pass impurity further?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי a further question. Granted, חיבת הקודש makes the item itself become disqualified, but does it also make the item count as a ראשון and a שני, so that it passes impurity on to other things?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Granted, the regard for holiness works to make the item itself disqualified. But should it also be called fully impure, so that we count a first and a second level of impurity from it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges how far רב כהנא's answer goes. He accepts part of it but questions a bigger result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Impure as food' suggests full food status, where impurity is counted in levels: a ראשון makes something a שני. רבינא agrees that חיבת הקודש can ruin the holy item itself. He doubts that this kind of impurity is strong enough to pass on to other items in a chain.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that... (accepts one point in order to challenge another)
To make the item itself disqualified
First and second levels of impurity

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Granted that regard for holiness works for them
to make the item itself disqualified,
should it also be called fully impure,
so that we count first and second levels with it?
phrases.notes: He means: if it becomes a ראשון, would whatever touches it become a שני?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: נְהִי דְּמַהְנְיָא לְהוּ חִיבַּת הַקּוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how far רב כהנא's answer in step 8 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'impure with the impurity of food' when it is explained through חיבת הקודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חיבת הקודש may disqualify the item itself, but full food impurity means counting levels, and that may go beyond what חיבת הקודש can do.

steps.title: That would solve ריש לקיש's open question
steps.stepSummary: If we simply assumed that impurity from חיבת הקודש counts levels, we would have solved ריש לקיש's open question about the dry flour of a מנחה. Since his question was never settled, it seems we cannot assume it here either. The next step answers this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then resolve the question ריש לקיש asked: with dry flour of a meal offering, do we count first and second levels of impurity, or do we not count first and second levels?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבינא's doubt by pointing to an unsolved question of ריש לקיש about the very same issue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dry flour of a מנחה never touched liquid, so it can become impure only because of חיבת הקודש. ריש לקיש asked whether such impurity counts levels, and his question was never answered. The challenge is that if נותר and the פרה counted levels through חיבת הקודש, his question would already be solved. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Then resolve it, meaning: if so, you would have answered an open question
A dry portion of a meal offering's flour that never touched liquid
Do we count levels of impurity with it

steps.whatToRemember: Impurity that comes only from חיבת הקודש surely disqualifies the holy item itself. Whether it passes on in levels (ראשון, שני) on the Torah level is ריש לקיש's unsolved question about dry flour of a מנחה. The next step shows why that does not block our case.

phrases.english: Then resolve the question that Reish Lakish asks:
dry flour of meal offerings,
do we count first and second levels with it,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין מוֹנִין בּוֹ רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי?
phrases.english: or do we not count first and second levels with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבינא's doubt in step 9 by tying it to ריש לקיש's unsolved question.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assuming that impurity from חיבת הקודש counts levels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were clear, ריש לקיש's question about dry flour of a מנחה would already be answered, but it remains an open question.

steps.title: Torah level versus rabbinic level
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that ריש לקיש's unsolved question was about Torah law, while our case is about rabbinic law, so his open question does not stop us.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ריש לקיש had his doubt, it was about Torah law. When we said that impurity from חיבת הקודש counts as a ראשון and a שני, we were talking about rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 10 by showing that the two questions are on different levels of law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 argued: if we assume חיבת הקודש makes levels of impurity, ריש לקיש's question would already be solved. The answer is that ריש לקיש asked about Torah law, but our discussion of נותר and the פרה אדומה is about rabbinic law. So we can say it works on the rabbinic level and still leave ריש לקיש's Torah-level question open.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
By rabbinic law
He had a doubt, he raised a question

steps.whatToRemember: The same question can have one answer on the Torah level and another on the rabbinic level. Here, ריש לקיש's Torah-level doubt stays open, but on the rabbinic level חיבת הקודש does make the item a ראשון and a שני.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not solve ריש לקיש's question. It only shows that our case does not depend on it.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ – דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: When Reish Lakish raises the dilemma, it is by Torah law;
phrases.notes: This is his question from Step 10 about the dry flour of a מנחה.

phrases.english: when we said it, it was by rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: "We said" means our discussion about נותר and the פרה אדומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ – דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by level of law (Torah versus rabbinic)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying חיבת הקודש creates levels of impurity would automatically settle ריש לקיש's open question.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש asked about Torah law. Our case is rabbinic, so the two do not depend on each other.

steps.title: Vowed one kind of pan, brought the other
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a person vows a מנחה in a מחבת and brings it in a מרחשת, or the reverse, the offering is valid, but he has not kept his vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says, 'I take on myself a מנחה made in a מחבת,' and brings one made in a מרחשת, or says 'in a מרחשת' and brings one in a מחבת, what he brought is a valid offering. But he has not fulfilled his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with someone who promised one kind of pan and then used the other kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הרי עלי" is a general promise to bring a מנחה, not a promise about specific flour. So whatever he brought is still a good voluntary offering. But it is not the type he promised, so he still owes a מנחה in the pan he named.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (written here as מַתְנִי׳)
"It is on me," a general promise to bring an offering
A shallow pan used for a מנחה
A deep pan used for a מנחה
What he brought counts as a valid offering
He has not fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who says: "It is upon me in a shallow pan"
phrases.notes: He means: I take on myself to bring a מנחה made in a מחבת.

phrases.english: and he brought it in a deep pan;
or "in a deep pan" and he brought it in a shallow pan,
what he brought, he brought,
but he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he made a general promise (הרי עלי) and switched the type of pan, the offering is valid as a voluntary offering, but he still owes his vow.

steps.title: Specific flour set aside for one pan, made in the other
steps.stepSummary: If he points to specific flour and says 'this' is for a מחבת, and then makes it in a מרחשת, or the reverse, the offering is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'This is to be brought in a מחבת,' and brought it in a מרחשת, or 'in a מרחשת' and brought it in a מחבת, the offering is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. This time he set aside a specific portion of flour instead of making a general promise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is "זו" (this). Here the promise is attached to this exact flour and the pan he named for it. Making that flour in a different pan goes against what he declared about it, so the offering itself is פסולה, not just 'not his obligation.'

keyTerms.meaning: "This": he set aside a specific portion
Not valid, disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 12. With הרי עלי (a general promise) the offering counts but he still owes his vow. With זו (this specific flour) the offering itself is פסולה.

phrases.english: "This is to be brought in a shallow pan," and he brought it in a deep pan;
phrases.notes: "This" points to a specific tenth of an איפה of flour he set aside.

phrases.english: or "in a deep pan," and he brought it in a shallow pan,
this offering is not valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares with Step 12: specific flour (זו) instead of a general promise (הרי עלי).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Specific flour set aside for one pan and made in the other is פסולה.

steps.title: Vowed one vessel, brought two, or the reverse
steps.stepSummary: If he vows two עשרונות in one vessel and brings them in two vessels, or the reverse, the offering counts, but he has not kept his vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I take on myself two עשרונות to bring in one vessel,' and brings them in two vessels, or says 'in two vessels' and brings them in one vessel, what he brought counts. But he has not fulfilled his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third case. It follows the same pattern as Step 12, but now the switch is the number of vessels instead of the type of pan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Promising one vessel means one מנחה of two עשרונות. Promising two vessels means two separate מנחות. Switching between them gives him a valid offering, but not the one he promised, so he still owes it.

keyTerms.meaning: Two tenths of an איפה of flour
One vessel, meaning one single מנחה
Two vessels, meaning two separate מנחות

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule: a general promise (הרי עלי) brought the wrong way still counts as an offering, but he must bring what he promised. Specific flour (זו) made the wrong way is פסולה.

phrases.english: One who says: "It is upon me to bring two tenths

phrases.aramaic: לְהָבִיא בִּכְלִי אֶחָד״, וְהֵבִיא בִּשְׁנֵי כֵּלִים,
phrases.english: in one vessel," and he brought them in two vessels;
or "in two vessels," and he brought them in one vessel,
what he brought, he brought,
but he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר: ״הֲרֵי עָלַי שְׁנֵי עֶשְׂרוֹנוֹת לְהָבִיא בִּכְלִי אֶחָד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of Step 12 to a switch in the number of vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Switching between one vessel and two vessels gives a valid offering, but he has not fulfilled his vow.

steps.title: Pointing at specific flour for one vessel or two, then switching
steps.stepSummary: If he points at flour and says 'these' are for one vessel and brings them in two, or the reverse, the offerings are פסולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'These are for one vessel,' and brings them in two vessels, or says, 'These are for two vessels,' and brings them in one vessel, they are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה takes the one-vessel/two-vessel case from Step 14 and applies the 'pointing' rule from Step 13 to it. When he points at specific flour and then switches the number of vessels, the offerings are פסולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14 he made a general vow ('הרי עלי'), so the offering still counted and only his vow was left unfulfilled. Here he said 'אלו', 'these', so he gave this exact flour a specific identity. Switching from one vessel to two, or two to one, goes against that identity, so the offering itself is ruined.

keyTerms.meaning: 'These': he points at specific flour and gives it a fixed identity
Vessel: here it means one מנחה offering. One vessel means one מנחה, and two vessels means two
Invalid: the offerings are not accepted

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 14. There it said 'הרי עלי' (a general vow), so the offering was valid. Here it says 'אלו' (pointing at flour), so the offering is invalid.

phrases.english: 'These are in one vessel,' and he brought them in two vessels;
phrases.notes: He means two עשרונות of flour sitting in front of him, which he pointed at as one מנחה.

phrases.english: or 'in two vessels,' and he brought them in one vessel:
these are invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ בִּכְלִי אֶחָד וְהֵבִיא בִּשְׁנֵי כֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'pointing makes it פסול' rule from Step 13 to the vessel-count case of Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he points at specific flour as one or two מנחות and then changes the number of vessels, the offerings are פסולין.

steps.title: Vowed one vessel, brought two, and was reminded
steps.stepSummary: He vowed two עשרונות in one vessel and brought them in two. Others told him, 'You vowed one vessel.' If he still offers them in two vessels, they are פסולין. If he offers them in one vessel, they are כשרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'It is upon me to bring two tenths in one vessel,' and brings them in two vessels, and people tell him, 'You vowed in one vessel,' then if he offers them in two vessels they are invalid, and if in one vessel they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new detail to the general-vow case: before he offers the flour, others remind him of what he vowed. What he does after the reminder decides the result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a reminder (Step 14), bringing two vessels just meant he had not kept his vow, but the offering still counted. Once he is reminded and still offers in two vessels, he is treating it as his vow while going against it, so it becomes פסול. If he listens and brings it in one vessel, he has kept his vow and it is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Tenths of an איפה, the measure of flour for a מנחה
'You vowed': the reminder people give him about his original promise
He offered them on the altar
Valid: the offerings are accepted

steps.whyThisMatters: The same physical act (bringing two vessels) can lead to two different outcomes. It depends on whether he was reminded of his vow and still went ahead.

phrases.english: 'It is upon me to bring two tenths'

phrases.aramaic: לְהָבִיא בִּכְלִי אֶחָד״, וְהֵבִיא בִּשְׁנֵי כֵּלִים,
phrases.english: 'to bring in one vessel,' and he brought them in two vessels,
and they said to him: 'You vowed in one vessel.'
If he offered them in two vessels, they are invalid;
in one vessel, they are valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי עָלַי שְׁנֵי עֶשְׂרוֹנוֹת לְהָבִיא בִּכְלִי אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the general-vow case of Step 14 and adds a reminder before he offers it, which changes the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After being reminded that he vowed one vessel, offering in two vessels makes the offering פסול. Offering in one vessel is כשר.

steps.title: Vowed two vessels, brought one, and was reminded
steps.stepSummary: He vowed two עשרונות in two vessels and brought them in one. After being reminded, if he offers them in two vessels they are כשרין. If he put them into one vessel, they are treated like two מנחות that got mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'It is upon me to bring two tenths in two vessels,' and brings them in one vessel, and people tell him, 'You vowed in two vessels,' then if he offers them in two vessels they are valid. If he put it into one vessel, it is like two מנחות that became mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the reverse of Step 16. Going back to two vessels is כשר. Putting everything into one vessel is not simply called פסול; instead it is judged by the rule for two מנחות that got mixed together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flour vowed as two separate מנחות keeps the identity of two offerings even if he puts it all in one vessel. So the case is handled like two separate מנחות that got mixed together, which is a category the halacha already has a rule for.

keyTerms.meaning: He put it, meaning he placed all the flour into one vessel
Two מנחות that became mixed together, a case that already has its own rule

steps.whatToRemember: 'אלו' (pointing at flour) plus a change makes the offering פסול. 'הרי עלי' (a general vow) plus a change: the offering counts, but the vow is not kept. After a reminder: going against the vow makes it פסול, and keeping the vow makes it כשר. Two vessels squeezed into one is treated like two mixed מנחות.

phrases.english: 'It is upon me to bring two tenths'

phrases.aramaic: לְהָבִיא בִּשְׁנֵי כֵּלִים״, וְהֵבִיא בִּכְלִי אֶחָד,
phrases.english: 'to bring in two vessels,' and he brought them in one vessel,
and they said to him: 'You vowed in two vessels.'
If he offered them in two vessels, they are valid;
if he put it into one vessel,
it is like two meal offerings that became mixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי עָלַי שְׁנֵי עֶשְׂרוֹנוֹת לְהָבִיא בִּשְׁנֵי כֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror-image case of Step 16: vowed two vessels, brought one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering in two vessels after the reminder is כשר. Putting it all in one vessel is judged like two מנחות that became mixed.

steps.title: The גמרא opens: both kinds of change needed to be taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by saying 'וצריכא': the משנה had to teach both the מחבת/מרחשת change and the one-vessel/two-vessel change.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה by saying it really needed both kinds of cases. This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא will explain why one case could not be learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave two kinds of change with the same result: the offering counts, but the vow is not kept. One kind changed the pan (Step 12), and the other changed the number of vessels (Step 14). It looks like one of them would have been enough. 'וצריכא' says no: each case teaches something the other could not, and the explanation is about to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that comes after the משנה
'And it is necessary': both cases had to be taught, because neither could be learned from the other

phrases.english: GEMARA: And it is necessary.
phrases.notes: It was necessary to teach both changes: the pan type and the number of vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא, and opens by justifying why the משנה needed both kinds of change.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the pan-type change and the vessel-count change had to be taught, because neither could be learned from the other.

steps.title: Why the pan-type case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה taught only the מחבת/מרחשת case, we might think a change in the number of vessels does not matter, so the vow would be fulfilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה had taught only the first case, we would say he fails because he promised a shallow pan and brought a deep pan. But where both the promise and the offering use the same kind of pan, we might think he fulfilled his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of its צריכא. It shows why the vessel-count case had to be taught even though the pan-type case was already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing from מחבת to מרחשת is a change in the kind of offering, so failing the vow there seems obvious. Changing only the number of vessels keeps the same kind of pan, so we could have thought it is a minor detail. The משנה teaches that even this change means he has not kept his vow.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught us (had the משנה taught us)
The first one (the first case)
This and that (both of them)
He fulfilled his vow

phrases.english: For if it had taught us only that first case,
[we would say he fails] because he said "in a shallow pan"
and he is bringing it in a deep pan;
but here, where both are in a shallow pan,
phrases.notes: 'Both' means what he promised and what he actually brought.

phrases.english: or both are in a deep pan,
I would say he has also fulfilled his vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the צריכא opened in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pan-type case alone would not teach that a change in vessel count also fails the vow.

steps.title: Why the vessel-count case alone would not be enough, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה taught only the vessel-count case, we might think he fails only because he split the flour. Changing the pan type without splitting might seem fine, so both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it had taught only this case, we would say he fails because he divided the flour. But in the pan case, where nothing is divided, we might say he does not fail. So both cases are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of the צריכא and closes it with 'צריכא', meaning both cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the vessel-count case, the reason for failing could be the splitting or joining of the flour. In the pan-type case, nothing is split, so we might have thought the vow is kept. Each case closes a gap the other leaves open.

keyTerms.meaning: Divides, splits
It is necessary (both teachings are needed)
I would say (our mistaken assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: Changing the kind of pan and changing the number of vessels are separate failures. Each one alone means he has not kept his vow.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only this case,
[we would say he fails] because he divides them,
but there, where he does not divide it,
I would say not. So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכא begun in step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה needed both the pan-type case and the vessel-count case, because neither can be learned from the other.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון holds the vow is fulfilled
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says the offering counts but the vow is not kept. רבי שמעון says the vow is fulfilled too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: what he brought counts as an offering, but he has not fulfilled his vow. רבי שמעון says: he has fulfilled his vow as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing a מחלוקת on the cases of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא agrees with the משנה: the changed offering is valid but does not pay off the vow. רבי שמעון disagrees and holds that these changes do not stop the vow from being fulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
His vow's obligation: what רבי שמעון says is fulfilled too

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree the offering itself is valid. They argue only about whether his vow is now paid off.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: what he brought, he brought,
but he has not fulfilled his vow.
Rabbi Shimon says:
He has even fulfilled his vow as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the צריכא, the גמרא brings a ברייתא showing a dispute on the same type of case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: the offering counts but the vow is not fulfilled. רבי שמעון: the vow is fulfilled too.

steps.title: Challenge: if the vessel did not sanctify it, why call it disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה calls flour set aside for a מחבת and brought in a מרחשת 'פסולה'. But a ברייתא says the כלי שרת did not sanctify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'This is to bring in a shallow pan' and if he brought it in a deep pan it is disqualified. But a ברייתא teaches that the service vessels did not sanctify it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a case from the משנה and challenges it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כלי שרת did not sanctify the flour at all, it should simply stay ordinary flour. So why does the משנה call it disqualified? That word suggests it has holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Service vessels of the Temple, which sanctify what is put in them
Sanctified them
But was it not taught in a ברייתא (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: "This is to bring in a shallow pan" —
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
The service vessels did not sanctify them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new question on the משנה's case from step 13: designated flour (זו) brought in the wrong pan.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that such flour is פסולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the כלי שרת did not sanctify it, it should stay ordinary flour and not be called disqualified.

steps.title: אביי: sanctified enough to be disqualified, not to be offered
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the vessel does not sanctify the flour to be offered on the מזבח, but it does sanctify it enough to become disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the vessels did not sanctify it to be offered, but they did sanctify it to become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by saying the vessel sanctifies the flour in a partial way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא means the flour cannot be offered from this vessel. But it still gets enough holiness to be called פסולה, so the משנה and the ברייתא do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: To be offered on the מזבח
To become disqualified

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי שרת can give partial holiness: enough to make an offering פסולה, even when not enough to let it be offered.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that holiness from a vessel has levels. Being 'sanctified to be disqualified' is a lower level than being 'sanctified to be offered'.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They did not sanctify them to be offered,
but they did sanctify them to become disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting levels of holiness: sanctified for disqualification, not for offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to mean the flour gets no holiness at all and stays ordinary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The flour gets enough holiness to become פסולה, but not enough to be offered.

steps.title: אביי opens a statement limiting the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins a new teaching with 'לא שנו', a signal that he is about to narrow the משנה's ruling to a specific case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: They only taught this...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move: אביי starts a second statement about the same משנה with 'לא שנו', and the actual limit will come right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra 'ו' in 'ואמר' tells us this is another statement by the same אביי who just answered the קשיא in Step 23. The phrase 'לא שנו' does not bring a new ruling by itself. It announces that the ruling about the מנחה brought in the wrong pan does not apply to every case, only to the one he is about to describe.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'they did not teach'. A standard opener meaning 'this ruling was only said about a certain case'.
'They taught', referring to the חכמים of the משנה
The full pattern this usually becomes: 'they only taught this when...', which limits a ruling

steps.confusionAlert: 'לא שנו' does not mean the משנה never taught this ruling. It means the ruling holds only in a specific situation, which אביי is about to name.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
They taught [this ruling] only...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the קשיא in Step 23, the same אביי now adds a separate teaching that narrows when the משנה's ruling applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי announces that the משנה's ruling about a מנחה brought in a different pan applies only in a specific case, which he will name next.
